item.text: {"text":"Long-/short-term fusion has clear precedents. [SHAN (IJCAI 2018)](https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/2018/0546.pdf) attention-pools historical items into a dynamic long-term representation, then attention-pools that representation with recent items; this is attention-based fusion, rather than sigmoid gating. Its experiments use Tmall/Gowalla, not Amazon. [HGN (KDD 2019)](https://arxiv.org/html/1906.09217) combines a learned long-term user embedding, user-conditioned feature/instance gates over recent items, average pooling, and additive item–item scores. Amazon Books Recall@10 ablations: feature-gate+average 0.0361, instance-gate+average 0.0351, both gates+average 0.0391, both+max 0.0355, full HGN 0.0429. These support pooling and item–item contributions, but lack an ungated mean-pooling control isolating gating. HGN versus SASRec Recall@10: Books 0.0429/0.0358; CDs 0.0426/0.0341. Training differs: HGN uses five-item inputs, three targets, BPR and batch 4096; SASRec uses length 50 and batch 128.\n\nSimple recency aggregation and normalization deserve separate controls. [HAM](https://arxiv.org/html/2002.11890) combines user embeddings with mean-pooled longer/recent windows; under leave-three-out, ungated HAM-mean beats HGN on CDs Recall@10 (0.0669/0.0600), while SASRec beats both on Books (0.0958 versus 0.0783/0.0665). This challenges gating’s necessity, although architectural differences prevent causal attribution. [ANIIP](https://peerj.com/articles/cs-867.pdf) reports CDs/Books Recall@10: plain item–item model 0.0489/0.0450; recency attenuation 0.0527/0.0482; full model 0.0554/0.0529; without normalization 0.0490/0.0465; without HGN initialization 0.0532/0.0518. Its normalization transforms item–item matching scores, not LayerNorm. These published protocols differ from the pinned sampled HR@10 benchmark; they establish precedents, not expected gains. Under fixed training settings, compare mean/recency pooling, fixed versus learned fusion, gating, and normalization independently."}
